items.title: Detect and consume runner jobs SSE as a notification hint
items.context: Add CLI authority runner logic that opens /v1/runners/{runnerId}/jobs/stream when live authority mode is active, parses jobs.available events, and triggers the existing signed claim path without treating the event as ownership proof.

happy.desc: A live authority runner with valid customer key and runner identity receives a jobs.available SSE event and immediately attempts the existing signed claim path.

edge.desc: If the stream returns a single snapshot with no jobs, disconnects, times out, or is not text/event-stream, the CLI falls back to existing polling without blocking the runner forever.

adversarial.desc: A jobs.available event is never treated as a leased job; the CLI must still require claim success before execution and must not claim productionDone or receipt verification from SSE alone.

items.userSees: Smoke output includes "GET /v1/runners/runner-1/jobs/stream" before "POST /v1/runners/runner-1/jobs/claim", and the result still reports claim success only after the signed claim response.

items.title: Preserve auth, retry, and host-neutral provider boundaries
items.context: Ensure Authorization/customer-key handling, runner provider configuration, reconnect/backoff, and diagnostics stay consistent with authority_enforce_runner and autopilot authority paths. SSE auth failures, diagnostics, logs, and verification evidence must never expose raw Authorization headers or customer API keys.

happy.desc: The SSE request carries the same Authority customer API key source as other protected Authority reads and works for codex/claude runner identities without provider-specific shortcuts.

edge.desc: 401/403/404/server-unavailable stream failures produce a clear readiness/fallback diagnostic and continue through the configured safe fallback path where appropriate, without printing raw Authorization headers or customer API keys.

adversarial.desc: Provider-specific or host-specific assumptions cannot bypass runner registration, heartbeat, session binding, claim ownership, existing execution boundaries, or secret redaction for Authorization/customer API key material.

items.title: Document server dependency and client fallback contract
items.context: Update CLI-facing docs so developers understand that SSE improves notification latency only when the server supports long-lived job push, and that polling fallback remains the compatibility path.

happy.desc: Docs state how the CLI uses runner jobs SSE, what server capability is required, and how fallback behaves.

edge.desc: Docs clarify that retired Orchestrate is read-only legacy evidence and canonical proofbound is the mutating development root.

adversarial.desc: Docs do not overclaim faster provider execution, Authority completion, productionDone, or server-side push support before the server endpoint actually provides it.
